title: Testing functions separately
goal: Test a numerical computation independently of input and output.

prerequisites.text: Call an independent function and choose boundary values.

terms.title: Pure function
terms.definition: Returns a value from arguments without changing outside objects or printing.

terms.title: Test driver
terms.definition: Calls a function with known inputs and compares the results.

sections.title: Why it matters
paragraphs: Check a power limiter before building its interface by calling the computation with known numbers.
Write expected values before execution. A function contract and a presentation check are separate layers.

A boundary value helps when the adjacent branches produce distinguishable results. In clamp50, both branches can return exactly 50. In bonus, the driver’s output can expose a changed result at the boundary.

sections.title: Worked example
paragraphs: Check −5, 70 and 50. The computations are independent of evaluation order inside printf.

sections.title: Diagnostics
paragraphs: At input 50, x > 50 and x >= 50 select different branches. Both branches of clamp50 return 50 for that input. In the bonus task, taking the inclusive branch at 50 changes the result from 0 to 5.
The driver compares a returned value with the expectation. A function with a void return type supplies no value.

sections.title: Transfer to practice
paragraphs: The bonus driver reports the exact argument and mismatched expectation. The calculation itself prints nothing.
The value returned by bonus depends only on score, so the same argument gives the same result in any test order.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Test a numerical computation independently of input and output.

feedback: The lower limit applies to negative values.

selfcheck.prompt: The bonus is 5 for a score of at least 50 and 0 otherwise. For which input does using > in place of >= change the return value?
feedback: The inclusive condition gives a bonus of 5 at 50. Strict > leaves it at 0.

selfcheck.prompt: How can the check survive a change in presentation format?
selfcheck.feedback: Call the function from a separate driver and compare the returned value. A different main format does not change the call contract.

static void result(void) {}
int main(void) { return result() == 5; }

practice.title: Bonus at the threshold
practice.task: bonus returns 5 for a score of at least 50, otherwise 0. No input is needed. Fix the comparison and confirm calls with 49, 50 and 51 using the supplied driver.
practice.hint: Inspect the line for 50 in the starter. It shows the expected result and the observed one.
criteria: The driver prints passed 3 and exits with status 0.
The calculation neither reads input nor prints output.

steps.action: Leave the input empty and run the starter. Look at the result for 50.
steps.why: Test a numerical computation independently of input and output.
steps.expected: The driver prints fail 50 expected 5 got 0 and passed 2, then exits with status 1.

steps.action: Fix the condition in bonus and run the same test driver again.
steps.why: The change must satisfy the contract.
steps.expected: The driver prints 49 0, 50 5 and 51 5 in order, followed by passed 3, and exits with status 0.

steps.action: Check a distinct boundary case and explain the result.
steps.why: Different cases distinguish the parts of the rule.
steps.expected: The calculation neither reads input nor prints output.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: In a copy, set the threshold to 60 and design three tests around it.
criteria: Record all three expectations before executing.

teaching.scene: Before connecting a power controller, test its function with known values. Inputs on both sides and at the boundary help identify which part of the rule ran.

predict.prompt: The driver calls clamp50 with −5, 70 and 50. What comes back for each input, and which line can you verify?
predict.answer: −5 is below zero, so it returns 0. 70 exceeds the upper bound and returns 50. Exactly 50 is returned unchanged. The output is 0 50 50.

apply.prompt: Choose expected results for −1, 34 and 51. Which check detects a function that changes a reading already in range?
apply.answer: Expect 0, 34, 50. The input 34 should be preserved. A different result exposes a problem within the allowed range.

practice.strategy: Write the expected outcomes for 49, 50 and 51 before execution. Use the supplied driver to compare them and inspect the exact-boundary case separately.
practice.diagnosis: If 49 and 51 pass and 50 gives 0, the defect is at equality. Compare the bonus predicate with the wording of its lower bound.

syntax.explanation: A test driver supplies known input, compares the return value with an independently calculated expectation and reports mismatches.
syntax.mistake: One passing edge case covers only that input. Add the exact boundary between its two neighbors.
